exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
outcome: Gastrointestinal tract colonization and succession of bacteria, archaea, and microeukaryotes
cohort: Infants followed for the first year of life
finding: Cesarean section-delivered infants experienced a delay in colonization and succession of bacteria, archaea, and microeukaryotes compared to vaginally delivered infants.
mod_finding: Cesarean section-delivered infants had a delay in colonization and succession of bacteria, archaea, and microeukaryotes, with shifts in prokaryotic succession apparent as early as days 3 and 5 postpartum.
